Alex Chen: FYI — CloudLift procurement pinged about how marketplace SKUs map to our committed rate cards. They need an invoice sample that matches their PO fields. Anyone done this recently?
Maria Patel: Yup, did a mapping for a similar deal last quarter. Marketplace SKUs don't always line up 1:1 with our internal rate_card ids. Can share mapping.
Maria Patel: Example mapping I used:
```
marketplace_sku: RWF-HOST-STD -> internal_plan: hosted_standard -> rate_card: RC-2024-HOST-STD
marketplace_sku: RWF-DED-POOL -> internal_plan: dedicated_pool -> rate_card: RC-2024-DED-BASIC
```
Maria Patel: Note: marketplace shows gross price. If we commit a discount/rebate on our side we record it via contract rebate (not by changing SKU price in marketplace).
Jamal Owens: Important: revenue flow differs. If CloudLift buys through AWS Marketplace, the invoice comes from AWS (or from partner if we use listing type). That affects how finance maps the PO to our commitments. We need to confirm whether they want "list price on invoice = committed price" or a separate credit line.
Priya Rao: Procurement asks for line-level PO fields: PO number, "bill-to" legal name, tax ID, and cost center. Marketplace invoices often lack our internal cost center field — we had to provide invoice reconciliation docs for the last deal.
Emilia (Marketplace Ops): For AWS and GCP marketplaces we can include a customer-facing invoice id but we cannot arbitrarily add custom fields to the marketplace invoice. We can provide a seller-side reconciliation CSV that maps marketplace invoice lines to our rate_card rows.
Alex Chen: So options are: (A) recommend CloudLift buy direct (hosted API) so invoice comes from us and matches PO fields, (B) buy via marketplace but we provide reconciliation + a contract that guarantees net pricing, or (C) set up out-of-band invoicing for committed portion. Which is feasible?
Katie - Deal Desk: All three are feasible. Deal desk checklist: signed MSA + SOW, approved deviation for "out-of-band invoicing" if using marketplace, and Finance signoff for revenue recognition path. For (B) we'll need a rebate schedule attached to the contract showing effective net rates. Approvals: Revenue Ops + Legal.
Nora Legal: If we attach a rebate/credit outside marketplace, add clear language on invoicing party, payment path, and how credits are applied. Also flag export/data residency if CloudLift wants regional billing.
Jamal Owens: Billing detail — if we do out-of-band credits we need a mechanism for applying monthly credits against marketplace settlements. That requires our finance team to reconcile monthly and raise a credit memo. Takes ~2 weeks to automate; manual credit is possible short-term.
billing-bot: Invoice sample generated: https://internal.redwood.co/invoices/sample_marketplace_invoice_2024Q1.pdf (internal link)
Priya Rao: Procurement asked about term: they prefer a 12-month commit, annual invoice, Net30 payment terms, and vendor needs to accept PO referencing marketplace invoice id. Can we support Net30 on marketplace purchases?
Emilia (Marketplace Ops): Marketplace payment terms are typically determined by marketplace platform — merchants get paid on platform schedule. Customer-facing Net30 is possible if we invoice them outside marketplace, but that defeats the marketplace billing flow.
Maria Patel: For the POC we can suggest: 1) run initial 3-month POC purchased direct so invoices are clean, 2) roll to marketplace for seat/consumption after commit is signed, or 3) keep commit but handle committed-discount as a monthly credit reconciliation.
Alex Chen: CloudLift prefers to keep procurement inside their marketplace procurement flow for ease of PO mgmt. They asked if we can provide an "invoice mapping guide" + a short note for their AP team explaining how to match lines.
Katie - Deal Desk: I'll draft the invoice mapping guide and the clause for the contract that covers rebate application and reconciliation cadence. Will loop in Finance for the credit memo flow.
Nora Legal: I'll review the clause. Also want to ensure the contract calls out who issues refund/credit if there's an overpayment.
Jamal Owens: Action item for Finance: confirm how we post marketplace revenue and apply rebates in ledger — I can follow up with a ticket.
Alex Chen: Thanks — can we aim to have the mapping guide + sample invoice + recommended path (direct POC vs marketplace + credit flow) by tomorrow EOD? I'll schedule a 30m sync with CloudLift, Legal, and Procurement for 11am PT tomorrow.
Priya Rao: Works for procurement — please add the AP contact to the invite.
Maria Patel: I can run a quick demo of the billing alignment during the call.
Alex Chen: Perfect, thanks all :thumbsup:
